receipts.first_text_witness: Two women graduate the same year from the same state university. Same degree, same starting salary, $48,000 marketing coordinator, mid-size city, same rent, same monthly take home of about $3,100 after taxes. Their apartments are 3 miles apart. They get coffee at the same place on Sunday mornings. 10 years later, one of them opens her banking app on a Tuesday and checks her balance the way you'd check the weather, casually, no stakes. She has $47,000 in a brokerage account, a used 2021 Honda she owns outright, and a mortgage payment that fits inside her budget without touching the sides. The other one has three unread voicemails from a number she doesn't recognize. There's a drawer in her kitchen she hasn't opened since February because she knows what's in it. She makes $67,000 now, nearly $20,000 more than when she started, and she has less financial room than she did at 23.
